reason: After a host reboot every memory-runner job whose launch owner was a process of the old boot stayed charged forever, and a held job also blocked every coordinated shutdown (runtime-stop): MemoryReconciler._reconcile and MemoryBudgetService.release_prelaunch(owner_dead=True) both required the owner's recorded process origin to equal the current one. A parseable earlier kernel boot now proves the owner ended with its kernel on this host (process_identity.launch_owner_ended, shared by both checks); because a host sharing the database would look the same, the supervisor's reconciler also requires RuntimeProcessHost.boot_ended (no unretired runtime born on that boot still renews a lease), and project-worker reconcilers leave such jobs to it. Only never-launched reservations are released on that proof; starting and launched jobs keep the uncertain / verified-removal paths. The selection covers the reconciler, prelaunch release and its guards, host memory recovery, rediscovery/lease helpers and origin parsing, including 14 new regressions.
exclusions: Memory enforcement suites that need a container runtime are not selected (they are unchanged; this change only alters which owners count as ended). PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set; the selection passed locally on SQLite and PostgreSQL 16. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. The real-Core release of a previous-boot reservation and the unblocked runtime-stop are recorded in the PR.
